title: Paella Valenciana
subtitle: The original Valencia paella with chicken, rabbit, and vegetables
excerpt: Paella valenciana is the original paella from Valencia, made with chicken, rabbit, flat green beans, white beans, saffron, and short-grain paella rice. The defining characteristic is the socarrat: the layer of toasted, caramelised rice that forms on the base of the pan. Paella is a rice dish, not a meat or seafood dish.
sourceNotes: Paella originated in the region of Valencia and is documented from the 18th century. The name refers to the wide, shallow pan (from the Latin patella). The Valencian version uses chicken, rabbit, and vegetables. Seafood paella (paella de marisco) is a later development. The socarrat is not an accident. It is the most prized part of the dish.

content.text: Paella rice absorbs the stock and must not be stirred after it is added. Unlike risotto, the rice in paella is never agitated: the goal is individual, flavour-saturated grains with a dry, non-creamy texture. The socarrat (toasted crust) forms in the last 2 to 3 minutes: you will hear a crackling sound and smell a faintly toasty aroma.

items.prepNote: flat green beans (or French beans), cut into 4 cm lengths

content.text: Heat the olive oil in a wide paella pan or large frying pan over high heat. Season the chicken and rabbit with salt. Fry in batches for 5 to 6 minutes per side until deep golden. Remove and set aside.

Lower the heat to medium. Add the green beans to the pan and fry for 3 minutes. Add the garlic and the grated tomato. Cook, stirring, for 5 minutes until the tomato has reduced to a thick paste (the sofrito).
Add the sweet paprika and stir for 30 seconds. Return the meat to the pan. Pour in 1.2 litres of hot water (or chicken stock) plus the saffron-infused water. Season with salt. Bring to a boil.

Add the rice in a rain across the pan. Stir once to distribute, then do not stir again. Add the butter beans. Boil vigorously for 10 minutes, then reduce to a simmer for 8 to 10 minutes until the rice has absorbed the liquid and is cooked through.

Increase the heat to high for the final 2 minutes to create the socarrat. Listen for a faint crackling. Remove from the heat, cover with a clean cloth, and rest for 5 minutes. Serve at the table from the pan.

items.symptom: Rice is creamy rather than dry and separate
items.cause: The rice was stirred after being added
items.fix: Paella rice must not be stirred. Distribute it once when adding, then leave it. Stirring releases starch and produces a risotto texture.

items.symptom: Bottom of the rice burns rather than forming socarrat
items.cause: Heat was too high or the socarrat stage was left too long
items.fix: The socarrat stage lasts 2 minutes maximum. Listen for crackling and a toasty aroma. If you smell burning, remove immediately.
